title: Practice of Grassroots Organisations Transferring Sums of Money to Personal Bank Accounts for Official Operational Needs and Actions Taken
what_it_is: Practice of Grassroots Organisations Transferring Sums of Money to Personal Bank Accounts for Official Operational Needs and Actions Taken

sections.label: Questions on GRO money transfers
sections.summary: Questions asked the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth about GROs transferring money to personal bank accounts and related procedures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (a) over the last five years, what is the number of Grassroots Organisations (GROs) that have engaged in the practice of transferring sums of money to personal bank accounts for official operational needs and their respective amounts transferred; (b) in the case of the two GROs uncovered during the AGO's test checks, who are the responsible persons who authorised such transfers; and (c) what forms of disciplinary actions are taken against the relevant authorised persons.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth with regard to the Auditor-General's report that found inappropriate money management practices for welfare assistance schemes and in particular, the use of personal bank accounts to disburse cash for welfare and voucher assistance (a) what are the lessons learnt by the entities involved; and (b) whether systems will be put in place by those entities to prevent such occurrences in the future.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (a) what is the standard procedure to distribute monies to beneficiaries for programmes that are not yet covered by the Government's electronic voucher system; and (b) how will the People's Association ensure that this procedure will be adhered to.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth in light of the test checks in the latest Auditor-General's Office report finding that two grassroots organisations (GROs) had transferred significant sums of money to the personal bank accounts of staff (a) whether there are further checks and tests being carried out to identify if more such practices have occurred; and (b) what action is the People's Association taking across all its entities to ensure GRO monies are not co-mingled with staff's personal monies given the significant risk of loss or misappropriation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Each year, GROs help to administer about three to four national schemes across all constituencies.

sections.label: Local schemes benefit residents
sections.summary: These local schemes benefit at least 400,000 residents annually across Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: In total, these local schemes benefit at least 400,000 residents annually across Singapore.

sections.label: AGO audit of welfare schemes
sections.summary: For the FY2022/2023 audit, AGO audited welfare assistance schemes from 1 April 2019 to 31 May 2022, and two GROs adopted inappropriate money management practices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: For the FY2022/2023 audit of PA, the AGO chose to audit welfare assistance schemes for the period of 1 April 2019 to 31 May 2022, a large part of which coincided with the COVID-19 pandemic.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: In its audit, two GROs were identified to have adopted inappropriate practices in the management of monies.

sections.label: No loss or misappropriation found
sections.summary: The AGO reviewed the records and found no evidence of loss or misappropriation of funds, as in the first case.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The AGO has reviewed the records and found no evidence of loss or misappropriation of funds, as in the first case.

sections.label: PA counselled staff and volunteers
sections.summary: PA took note of the AGO's areas and observations and counselled its staff and volunteers involved to adhere strictly to governance processes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Nonetheless, we do not take this for granted, and to Mr Saktiandi Supaat and Dr Tan Wu Meng's questions, PA has taken note of the areas and observations by the AGO and has counselled its staff and volunteers involved of the need to adhere strictly to governance processes.

sections.label: PA to implement AGO recommendations
sections.summary: Going forward, PA will implement all of AGO's recommendations in the FY2022 and FY2023 reports.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Going forward, PA will implement all of AGO's recommendations in the FY2022 and FY2023 reports.

sections.label: PA independent review committee
sections.summary: PA set up an independent review committee, separate from staff and internal audit, to review AGO findings and strengthen the system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: In this respect, PA has also set up an independent review committee to review the latest AGO findings – independent from the existing staff and the internal audit team – to review the latest AGO findings and to ensure measures are put in to strengthen the system.

sections.label: Review committee membership and report
sections.summary: The committee has one board member and senior grassroots members not on the board or tied to senior management; publishing a report will be discussed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The committee has got one board member and other senior grassroots members who are not on the board and otherwise not connected to PA's senior management.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: In relation to the Member's point about whether we will make the findings public and publish a report, I will have a word with the review committee.

sections.label: Scope of checks
sections.summary: The checks' scope would be similar to the AGO's in timing and transactions, considering the nature of problems found.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The scope of the checks, as I said, would be similar to what the AGO has done in terms of timing as well as the scope – "scope" meaning the kind of transactions as well as having regard to the nature of the problems picked up.
